findings.title: Agent diverts to demo profile instead of reschedule
findings.evidence_quote: First, would you like to create a demo patient profile? I just need your first and last name to get started.
findings.what_happened: After the caller twice stated they needed to reschedule a specific Tuesday 2pm appointment and gave their desired window, the agent instead asked to create a 'demo patient profile' rather than addressing the reschedule.
findings.why_it_matters: This derails the call, forces the caller to repeat their request, and delays resolution of a time-sensitive scheduling conflict.
findings.expected_behaviour: The agent should have proceeded to look up the existing appointment or asked identifying details directly relevant to locating it, not introduced an unrelated 'demo profile' step.

findings.title: Agent invents a date of birth never provided
findings.evidence_quote: Your patient profile is set up. And your date of birth is 07/04/2000. How can I help you today?
findings.what_happened: The agent states a specific date of birth for the caller that was never given in the conversation, and the caller immediately confirms it is wrong.
findings.why_it_matters: Fabricating identifying patient information is a serious data-integrity failure that could lead to matching the wrong patient record or corrupting the correct one.
findings.expected_behaviour: The agent should never assert patient identifying details that were not supplied; it should ask the caller to provide or confirm date of birth.

findings.title: Agent fails to locate confirmed existing appointment
findings.evidence_quote: I don't see any upcoming appointments for you on the system. Would you like me to help you book a new appointment for Thursday or Friday after 3PM?
findings.what_happened: The caller clearly stated an existing Tuesday 2pm appointment with a confirmation received, but the agent reports no record and pivots to booking a new appointment without further identity verification attempts (e.g., asking for phone number, confirmation number, or correct DOB).
findings.why_it_matters: If the original appointment is not actually cancelled, the patient may end up double-booked or the old appointment may go unaddressed, causing confusion or a missed/duplicate visit.
findings.expected_behaviour: The agent should have asked for additional identifying information (correct DOB, phone number, confirmation number) before concluding the appointment does not exist, and should have addressed the fate of the original Tuesday appointment explicitly.

findings.title: Old Tuesday appointment cancellation never confirmed
findings.evidence_quote: Your appointment is confirmed for Friday, September 4 at 03:30PM with doctor Zbigniew Lacoste at Pivot Point Orthopaedics.
findings.what_happened: The final confirmation only addresses the new Friday appointment and never confirms whether the original Tuesday 2pm appointment (which the caller insists exists) was located, cancelled, or otherwise resolved.
findings.why_it_matters: The caller may believe their reschedule is complete while the original appointment remains active elsewhere in the system, risking a missed cancellation or duplicate booking.
findings.expected_behaviour: The agent should explicitly confirm the disposition of the original appointment (cancelled, or note that no record was found and advise the caller to verify) alongside confirming the new booking.

findings.title: Doctor's name changes across three consecutive turns
findings.evidence_quote: Your appointment is confirmed for Friday, September 4 at 03:30PM with doctor Zbigniew Lacoste at Pivot Point Orthopaedics.
findings.what_happened: The agent refers to the provider as 'doctor Zidmio Lukaske' in turn 020, 'doctor Zetmio Lukowski' in turn 022, and 'doctor Zbigniew Lacoste' in the final confirmation in turn 024 — three different names for what should be the same provider.
findings.why_it_matters: Inconsistent provider identification in a booking confirmation could cause the patient to arrive expecting the wrong doctor or doubt the reliability of the confirmation altogether.
findings.expected_behaviour: The agent should consistently state the same, correct provider name throughout the call and in the final confirmation.
